items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: you had to identify who wrote this, whether it was Bach or Beethoven or whoever, you know, was the composer.

ctx.x: Well a lot of the people we’ve talked to have talked about their great high school experience and it’s amazing the congregation of people that were in Chicago for instance, the famous names that all came out of there in that time period.

It was great. And that was the period when most of them came out. Because they had that music education. It was a part of the training that you got. You had to have that. Everybody had to have a certain amount of music. Everybody, in all the classes, no matter what your majors were, you had to have a music class. They called it music appreciation, where they’d play records of the, you know, the classical records, and you had to identify who wrote this, whether it was Bach or Beethoven or whoever, you know, was…
Yeah. If you were able to tell some future jazz star a couple words about what they should know about their own business. Do you have any thoughts on that?
